children.title: USDA and HHS Begin Review of Dietary Guidelines Scientific Report
children.description_medium: On March 11, 2025, the U. S.  Department of Agriculture and Department of Health and Human Services announced a line-by-line review of the 2025 Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee scientific report.  The agencies said the final Dietary Guidelines for Americans would be released by the statutory deadline.
children.description_long: On March 11, 2025, the U.S. Department of Agriculture and Department of Health and Human Services announced a line-by-line review of the 2025 Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee scientific report. The agencies said the final Dietary Guidelines for Americans would be released by the statutory deadline. This describes the review announcement and its stated process. It is separate from later personnel events and does not by itself establish that scientific research was altered, suppressed, or “gutted.” The supplied USDA release is the source for the date, the agencies’ announced review, and their stated timeline. The USDA announcement concerns the process for reviewing the advisory committee’s report; it does not establish an outcome of that review. The later reporting on Kevin Hall concerns his retirement and his allegation that officials interfered with research communications. HHS denied the allegation, so the dispute should remain attributed to both parties. The two events are close in subject matter but separate in date and kind: one is an agency process announcement, and the other is a researcher’s employment decision and public account. The supplied evidence does not date or substantiate the card’s other claims about budget proposals, CDC restructuring, local-food reductions, or grant terminations.
children.date_uncertainty: Event dates are identified in the supplied reporting; publication dates may be later.

children.title: NIH Researcher Kevin Hall Announces Retirement and Alleges Censorship
children.description_medium: In April 2025, longtime NIH nutrition researcher Kevin Hall announced that he would retire after 21 years and alleged that HHS officials had interfered with communication of his research.  The Washington Post and CBS News reported Hall’s allegation and HHS’s denial; HHS said it remained committed to unbiased research.
children.description_long: In April 2025, longtime NIH nutrition researcher Kevin Hall announced that he would retire after 21 years and alleged that HHS officials had interfered with communication of his research. The Washington Post and CBS News reported Hall’s allegation and HHS’s denial; HHS said it remained committed to unbiased research. The claim of interference is therefore presented as Hall’s allegation, alongside the department’s response, rather than as an independently established finding. This personnel episode followed the March announcement of a dietary-guidelines review but is distinct from it. The supplied reports do not substantiate the original card’s broader claims about proposed budgets, CDC restructuring, local-food cuts, or grant terminations. The USDA announcement concerns the process for reviewing the advisory committee’s report; it does not establish an outcome of that review. The later reporting on Kevin Hall concerns his retirement and his allegation that officials interfered with research communications. HHS denied the allegation, so the dispute should remain attributed to both parties. The two events are close in subject matter but separate in date and kind: one is an agency process announcement, and the other is a researcher’s employment decision and public account. The supplied evidence does not date or substantiate the card’s other claims about budget proposals, CDC restructuring, local-food reductions, or grant terminations.
